sweep_summary: One sweep item. Glottolog 3623 'Obrst 1989, Transactions of the Royal Literary Fund 31: 147-185' is a corrupted OZBIB entry; Google Books records of the volume and of Bulletin signalétique 524 (1989) show the paper is Obrst, Leo, 'Stress and stress-related phenomena in Djinang', Texas Linguistic Forum 29 (Dec. 1988): 147-185 — a 39-page metrical-phonology (grid, lexical-cyclic) reanalysis of Djinang stress built on Waters 1980b's data. It is directly about Djinang word stress but no open copy exists (Google Books/HathiTrust snippet-only, absent from Crossref/OpenAlex/S2/archive.org); priority high to obtain via library (UT Austin TLF back issue). No snippet states stress placement, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the catalog yet. I fetched sources the catalog's own sources from the SEAlang Pacific Linguistics mirror (PL A-60 = Waters 1980b; PL C-114 = Waters 1989) and read the stress sections: primary stress normally word-initial, with a ~2% class of second-syllable stress driven by /a/ after a high-vowel initial syllable (§5.5, pp.38-40) and by durative reduplication; the catalog quote is verbatim but its first passage is on p.18, not p.17. new_statements.citation: Waters, Bruce E. 1980b. Djinang phonology. In B. Waters & P. Busby (eds), Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 14, 1-71. Pacific Linguistics A-60. Canberra: ANU.
new_statements.locator: pp.18, 29-30, 38-40 (PDF pages 24, 35-36, 44-46 of PL-A60); §5.1 Stress groups and rhythm, §5.5 Non-initial stress, §7.1 rules
new_statements.reading: Primary stress is word-initial by default (first syllable of the first stress group); a lexically restricted stress-shift rule moves primary (and secondary) stress one syllable rightward onto /a/ when the initial syllable has a high vowel and no intervening voiceless stop (about 2% of words, plus six unexplained residue words), and durative reduplication also yields non-initial primary stress. Secondary stresses fall on the first syllable of each following stress group (1-3 syllables, cluster-bounded). This is the catalog's own deciding source read first-hand; it confirms 'fixed initial' with a small /a/-attraction exception class. Two refinements: the 'normally have primary stress on the first syllable' sentence is on printed p.18 (not p.17), and the §5.5 two-percent second-syllable class should be noted. Waters 1989 (PL C-114, p.xv) agrees: 'non-contrastive vowel length may occur in the primary-stressed syllable, which is usually the first syllable of a word.'
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences

audit.reasoning: The coding (primary stress word-initial, weight-blind; secondary on stress-group-initial syllables; ~2% lexical shift to syllable 2 under i/u + a) rests on the dedicated 71-pp phonology of the language by its main describer, held as PDF+text, with every deciding quotation confirmed verbatim; the author's 1989 reference grammar (also held) restates the same generalisation at p.xvi. No newer or instrumental treatment of Djinang stress exists in Glottolog, OpenAlex or CrossRef. Only fix worth making: the locator 'sec.3.4 p.17' should read p.18 (printed page; PDF p.24 of). Nothing fetched sources; no audit directory needed. {pdf,txt}.
